title: Formation
description: Battle formation rules, troop-split templates and hero positioning.
sources: Kingshot hero/formation guides (context), shared by user

entries.name: Balanced (50/20/30)
entries.summary: Most versatile all-purpose formation, balancing defense and offensive pressure. Recommended default for players who want reliability across situations.

entries.name: Defensive (60/40/0)
entries.summary: High-durability, high-mobility defensive specialization popular with high-level players. Skips Archers entirely, letting you ignore Archer tech in the Academy and funnel resources into Infantry and Cavalry gear.

details.research_tip: Ignore Archer tech in the Academy to save resources; invest only in Infantry and Cavalry gear.

gen_5_powerhouse: Thrud (Infantry synergy makes the 60/40 defense nearly unbreakable)

entries.name: Offensive Whale-Killer (50/0/50)
entries.summary: Pure-destruction 'Cavalry Skip' build. Infantry holds the line while Archers melt the enemy. Designed for offensive rallies against high-power targets.

gen_3: Petra (used for her 'Dichotomy' skill buffing Infantry/Archer synergy, not her troops)
gen_5_apex: Vivian (S-tier for any Archer-heavy build; damage output reshapes the lineup at 5 stars)

entries.name: Mystic Trial formations by zone
entries.summary: Mystic Trial (PvE) has no single permanent ratio. Each of the six zones tests a DIFFERENT account system, so use the zone's baseline troop ratio and then adjust to the enemy lineup / the stage-10 wall. If troop-ratio changes barely move the result, the real bottleneck is that zone's stat system, not the ratio.

details.ratio_order: infantry/cavalry/archer (percent), matching this file's troop_split convention (same order as the Bear Hunt formations in events.json). The source wrote ratios as 'X/Y/Z' without labeling the order; infantry/cavalry/archer is the confirmed working assumption.
details.core_principle: Each zone tests a different part of your account. Upgrading the wrong system means changing troop ratios only hides the problem for a few stages.

zones.adjustment_rule: Shift toward your best-geared damage type if your front line survives.
zones.upgrade_priority: Hero quality, hero gear tiers and exclusive gear matter more than decorative account power.

zones.adjustment_rule: Do not overreact to troop type before checking pet skill value.
zones.upgrade_priority: Pet skills and combat-use pet development matter more than generic pet collection.

zones.adjustment_rule: If you lose too fast, improve charm breakpoints before testing exotic ratios.
zones.upgrade_priority: Use the Governor Charm Calculator before chasing the next charm level.

zones.adjustment_rule: Use a balanced setup unless your research is clearly skewed by troop type.
zones.upgrade_priority: Compare Academy and War Academy bottlenecks with the War Academy Calculator.

zones.adjustment_rule: Prioritize gear breakpoints before moving troops away from infantry safety.
zones.upgrade_priority: Use the Governor Gear Calculator to avoid spending on a weak breakpoint.

zones.adjustment_rule: Use your full account strength, then tune the ratio around the stage that blocks you.
zones.upgrade_priority: Fix your weakest full-account system rather than blaming one troop ratio.

stuck_stage_procedure: Do NOT immediately spend premium materials.

Run three cheap tests: (1) swap between the suggested ratio and one heavier-infantry setup; (2) try a slightly higher archer share if damage is missing; (3) check whether your weakest march is dragging the whole clear down.

If ratio changes barely move the result, the bottleneck is the zone's stat system (Coliseum=hero/gear, Crystal Cave=charms, Molten Fort=governor gear, Knowledge Nexus=research), so fix that system before spending.
Only then use the Mystic Trials Optimizer, before spending premium materials.
details.note: Ratios are starting points, not laws — adjust to the enemy lineup and the stage-10 wall.

entries.name: Core combat mechanics (troop counters)
entries.summary: How the three troop types interact, which drives every formation choice. Formation order is always Infantry / Cavalry / Archer (percent). A formation only works if you actually have enough of the required troop types.

details.infantry: The 'meat shield' — absorbs the initial waves of attacks and protects your damage dealers.
details.cavalry: Has a % chance to BYPASS infantry and directly hit archers, and deals INCREASED damage to archers. Use cavalry to counter enemy archer-heavy compositions.
details.archer: High damage/lethality but LOW defense against cavalry.
implications: Archers are generally less effective on DEFENSE than on attack (exposed to cavalry).
Sufficient infantry is vital to protect your damage dealers.
details.counter_triangle: Infantry shields -> Cavalry punishes exposed Archers -> Archers out-damage when protected.

entries.name: Recommended formations by scenario
entries.summary: Quick per-scenario troop splits (Infantry/Cavalry/Archer). Adjust to the enemy lineup and your available troop quantities. Cross-references existing detailed entries where they exist.

details.ratio_order: infantry/cavalry/archer (percent), matching this file's troop_split convention.

scenarios.why: Strong infantry front line, cavalry to counter enemy archers, archers for ranged damage. Same as entry balanced-50-20-30.

High infantry durability; cavalry cleans up any archers that slip through. Archers NOT recommended (weak on defense vs cavalry). Note: differs from the 60/40/0 in defensive-60-40-0 — this guide recommends 70/30/0 specifically for garrison.

Maximize lethality; archers have highest lethality, minimal inf/cav just to meet minimums. If 80% archers isn't possible, use max archers then prioritize cavalry (2nd-highest lethality). Matches events.json bear-hunt gen_3 (10/10/80); that entry has the full generation-by-generation ladder.
Balanced, versatile, robust — same as general rally joining.

entries.name: Formation slots and front/back line positioning
entries.summary: Most combat formations use 3 heroes with NO repeated troop category (1 infantry + 1 cavalry + 1 archer). A few modes allow 5 heroes with no category restriction. The battlefield always has 2 frontline slots and 3 backline slots.

five_hero_formations.rule: 5 heroes, NO troop-category restriction (can repeat categories).

open_questions: RESOLVED: see formation-slots (3-hero no-repeat for rally/pvp/garrison/bear; 5-hero no-restriction for arena/mystic; 2 frontline + 3 backline slots).
Star/gen recommendations above are from an external guide — reconcile hero picks against knowledge/hero_event_ratings.json where roles overlap.
